question.problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x+2y+5}.
$$

Using a substitution of the form $z=x+2y,$ transform the differential equation into an equation of the form ${z}^{′}(x)=f(z).$ What is the function $f(z)?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we make the substitution

$$
z=x+2y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=1+2\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-\frac{1}{2} & ={e}^{z+5}\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form ${z}^{′}(x)=f(z),$ we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=2{e}^{z+5}+1.
$$

Therefore, $f(z)=2{e}^{z+5}+1.$
